study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Zheng J, Zong X, Tang L, Guo H, Zhao P, Womer FY, Zhang X, Tang Y, Wang F (2024). Characterizing the distinct imaging phenotypes, clinical behavior, and genetic vulnerability of brain maturational subtypes in mood disorders. Psychological Medicine 54, 2774-2784.
study_identification_part.si4_title: Characterizing the distinct imaging phenotypes, clinical behavior, and genetic vulnerability of brain maturational subtypes in mood disorders

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: This study aimed to quantify brain morphological heterogeneity in mood disorders by mapping individual-level, region-specific gray matter volume (GMV) deviations from a normative model. It sought to identify patient subtypes through unsupervised clustering of these deviations and then to characterize and validate these subtypes using multi-modal data, including clinical behaviors, cell-specific transcriptomic profiles, and polygenic risk scores.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Individual deviation z-scores from the normative model, specifically from the 5th, 50th, and 95th percentiles. Subtyping was based on the 50th percentile deviation maps (z50 maps). Deviations were also categorized as infra-normal (z5 < -1.96) or supra-normal (z95 > 1.96).

caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: We then obtained individual-specific profiles of regional GMV deviations (z50 maps) to perform subtyping analysis... We defined the supra-normal as any individual exceeding the 95% CI for the 95th percentile (z95 > 1.96), and infra-normal as any individual below the 5% CI for the 5th percentile (z5 < -1.96).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Two-sample t-tests to compare clinical/cognitive scores between subtypes (FDR corrected). Graph theory-based network analysis of symptom correlations. Partial Least Squares (PLS) regression to associate GMV deviations with gene expression from AHBA. Logistic regression to analyze associations between subtypes and Polygenic Risk Scores (PRS) for MDD and AD.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Two distinct mood disorder subtypes were identified based on gray matter volume deviations: a 'supra-normal' subtype with increased frontal GMV, cognitive impairment, and higher Alzheimer's genetic risk, and an 'infra-normal' subtype with widespread decreased GMV, more severe depression, and higher MDD genetic risk.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Hierarchical clustering of individual GMV deviations in 174 mood disorder patients revealed two subtypes. Subtype 1 ('supra-normal', n=112) showed increased GMV in frontal cortex, poorer executive function on the WCST, and a higher polygenic risk score (PRS) for Alzheimer's disease (explaining up to 5.9% of variance). Their GMV patterns were spatially correlated with genes enriched for Alzheimer's pathways, endothelial cells, and oligodendrocytes. Subtype 2 ('infra-normal', n=62) showed globally decreased GMV, more severe depressive symptoms (higher HAMD scores, pFDR=0.025), a denser symptom network, and a higher PRS for major depressive disorder (explaining 10.8% of variance). Their GMV patterns were associated with genes related to microglia and inhibitory neurons. These distinct imaging phenotypes were replicable in an independent cohort (r=0.29 for subtype 1, r=0.45 for subtype 2).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: 1. Use of healthy brain gene expression data (AHBA) may not reflect patient-specific transcription. 2. Small sample size for genetic data. 3. Limited cognitive assessment (only WCST). 4. Inability to associate GMV alterations with first-episode symptom severity due to lack of specific data.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: There are several limitations to this work. First, the use of gene expression profiles from the healthy human brain in AHBA... Second, the genetic data size in our study was small... Third, we only used WSCT scores to test cognitive functions... Fourth, we did not obtain specific data about illness severity of the first episode...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study integrates multi-omics data (neuroimaging, transcriptomics, genetics) to define and validate biological subtypes that cut across traditional diagnostic boundaries of MDD and BD, providing a framework for precision medicine in mood disorders.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: A key innovation of this study is its trans-diagnostic approach, identifying neurobiological subtypes that are not aligned with the clinical diagnoses of MDD and BD. The distribution of MDD and BD diagnoses did not differ significantly between the two identified subtypes, suggesting the biological signatures are independent of the clinical labels. The study also uses a replication dataset to confirm the stability of the imaging phenotypes.
